messages.text: Lots of issues.  Device OS doesn’t match any pool data in regards to best difficulty.  Pools show negligible best difficulty <100 after days and device goes to 65.2k at boot up and just stays there and never changes.

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed this over to me.

Quick read on what you're seeing, then one thing I need from you.

On the Bitaxe/NerdQaxe-family firmware, "best difficulty" is an all-time record stored in flash. It loads back at boot and only changes when the device beats it. So a number that appears at boot and never moves usually means one of two things:

1. It's a leftover record from an earlier run (or factory burn-in) and nothing since has beaten it, or
2. the device is not actually submitting work to the pool at all, which would also explain the pool showing almost nothing after days.

The pool side showing best share under 100 after days is the part that worries me. That is the symptom to chase, not the 65.2k.

Two things so I can tell which it is:

1. Which model and which firmware version (exact string from the UI or the About screen)?
2. A screenshot of the device web UI main page, showing hashrate, shares accepted vs rejected, and the pool/stratum line.

If shares accepted is climbing but the pool sees nothing, it's a worker name or wrong stratum issue. If accepted is stuck at zero, it's a connection or difficulty issue on the pool side. The screenshot settles it in one step.
Searched the web · Hammer DC06 miner firmware 2.0.0 best difficulty
Searched the web · Hammer Miner DC06 330MH/s firmware download latest version

Thanks, that helps. Two things, and one correction to what I said before.

**Correction first:** the DC06 is the Scrypt (Litecoin/Dogecoin) unit, not a Bitaxe-family SHA-256 board, so forget my Bitaxe wording. The stored-record behaviour is the same idea though, and the mismatch you describe is still the real clue.

**Why 65.2k vs under 100 matters.** Those are two different numbers measured in two different places:

- The device's "best difficulty" is its own all-time record, kept in flash. It reloads at boot and only moves when the unit beats it.
- The pool's "best share" only counts shares the pool actually received from your worker.

At 330 MH/s the maths says you should be setting a new local best in the thousands roughly every day, so a value frozen at exactly 65.2k for days, while the pool sees under 100, reads as: the unit is not successfully submitting work, and the 65.2k is an old record carried over (quite possibly from factory test).

**Step 1, firmware.** You're on 2.0.0 (build 20260317). HammerMiner's own DC06 repo on GitHub currently publishes 
V3.0.0-20260916 as the latest DC06-APP release, with a V3.0.1-20260916 tag alongside it
. You are a full major version and about six months behind, and that is the first thing to clear before we chase anything else. Use only the vendor's own release (github.com/HammerMiner/DC06-APP). Do not flash any third-party image on a DC06, the community ones do not drive the MSBT0501 chips and the unit will boot but not hash.

**Step 2, what I need from you** (you can answer before or after the update):

1. Solo or pool mode, and the exact stratum URL and port you have in the dashboard?
2. What is the worker/accepted-shares counter on the device doing? Is it climbing, or sitting at zero?

If accepted shares are climbing on the device but the pool shows nothing, it is a worker name or stratum mismatch. If accepted is zero, it is the connection itself. That one answer splits it.

Solo mode.  Stratum. scrypt.mysolopool.com:3341
And to clarify the 65.2k best difficulty shows as since boot, not all time.
Good clarification, that changes the picture. Let me check one thing on that pool's ports before I answer.
Searched the web · mysolopool scrypt stratum port 3341 difficulty

That detail matters a lot. If it is "since boot" and it lands on 65.2k immediately and then never moves, that is not a record being set. A genuine best-since-boot starts small and climbs in steps. A number that is there at boot and frozen is almost always the difficulty the device was handed, being shown in the best-difficulty field.

I checked the pool's own setup page. Port 3341 is their variable-difficulty endpoint, the one they recommend for normal Scrypt ASICs. Username is your LTC address, then a dot or comma, then your DOGE address, optionally .worker. Password is `x` for vardiff, or `d=<number>` if you want a fixed difficulty.

So, three checks, in this order.

**1. The password field.** Does it contain just `x`, or does it have a `d=` number in it? If a fixed difficulty got set (65536 is the classic default), the pool would only ever accept a share at that level, and at 330 MH/s that is roughly one share every ten days. The pool would look almost dead, exactly as you describe. Set it to `x` and let vardiff do the work.

**2. The pool dashboard, not the device.** For your worker over the last 24 hours, what hashrate does the pool report, and what is the accepted share count? That single number splits this cleanly:

- Pool shows near 330 MH/s and shares accumulating: the hardware is fine and the device's difficulty display is just not what you think it is.
- Pool shows near zero hashrate: the unit is not delivering work and we have a real fault to chase.

**3. Firmware, still outstanding.** 2.0.0 (20260317) is a major version behind the vendor's current DC06-APP release, V3.0.0-20260916 on HammerMiner's own GitHub. Worth clearing regardless, since display bugs in the stats fields are exactly the kind of thing that gets fixed between majors.

Give me the answer to 1 and 2 and I can tell you which way this goes.

Understood, so vardiff is already set and it did not change anything.

Then check 2 is the one that decides this. On the pool dashboard for your worker, over the last 24 hours:

1. What hashrate does the pool report for that worker?
2. How many accepted shares?

Nothing from the device screen, only what the pool side says. That tells us whether the DC06 is actually delivering work or whether we are looking at a cosmetic stats bug in 2.0.0.

If the pool shows roughly 300 to 330 MH/s and shares ticking up, your hardware is working and the 65.2k field is just mislabelled or showing the assigned job difficulty, which the firmware update should sort.

If the pool shows near zero with a share count stuck, that is a real fault and I will want a short video of the device screen through a full boot plus a clear photo of the serial label, so I can put proper findings in front of our hardware lead.
Avg hashrate over 24 hours 292mh which looks ok on pool side

That number settles the main worry. 292 MH/s averaged over 24 hours against a 330 MH/s nominal rate is about 88 percent, and that is normal for a pool-side average on a solo pool. Shares arrive at random intervals, so a 24 hour average always lands a bit under nameplate. Your six MSBT0501 chips are hashing and the pool is receiving the work.

So: not a hardware fault. Nothing here points to a bad board, and I would not want you chasing an RMA over it.

What is left is the difficulty number itself, and I want to be straight with you about what I know and what I do not.

What I am fairly confident about:

1. With vardiff on 3341 the pool assigns you a low share difficulty. Many pool dashboards show that assigned difficulty in a column people read as "best difficulty". If the figure you are reading under 100 is the assigned vardiff level rather than your best share, the two numbers are not comparable at all and nothing is wrong.
2. Even if it is a genuine best share, beating 65.2k is rarer than it feels. At roughly 90 accepted shares a day, the odds of any one share topping 65.2k are about one in a thousand. That is a new record roughly every ten days, not daily. A flat reading for days is statistically ordinary.

What I cannot confirm: Scrypt has a long-standing convention split where difficulty is scaled by a factor of 65536 between implementations, and your device showing 65.2k is suspiciously close to that constant. That would make this a pure units mismatch between Thor OS and the pool. I will not state it as fact, because Thor OS is closed source and there is no published spec I can point you to for how that field is calculated.

Two things from here:

1. Update to the vendor's current DC06-APP release, V3.0.0-20260916 from HammerMiner's own GitHub. You are a major version behind, and stats-field behaviour is exactly what changes between majors.
2. I have put the difficulty-reporting question to JD, our hardware lead, with your model, firmware build and the pool figures.

Faster route if you want an answer before Monday: our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate. JD and a lot of DC06 owners are active there and someone will have compared the same two numbers.
Handed to the team · Cannot confirm how Thor OS calculates the best-difficulty field on the DC06; fir

That is with JD now. The team is offline over the weekend and picks this up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer comes to (email hidden)

In the meantime, the firmware update is the one thing worth doing yourself, and the Discord link above will likely get you a same-day answer from other DC06 owners.
Ok I will update os from hammer website to the newer one you referenced.

Good. A few things so it goes cleanly:

1. Source: the release I referenced is on HammerMiner's own GitHub, github.com/HammerMiner/DC06-APP, release V3.0.0-20260916. The vendor site links out to the same place. Only use that repo, nothing third party.
2. These units normally ship firmware in two parts, an APP image and a WWW image for the web interface. If the release has both, update both, and in the order the release notes give. Mismatched APP and WWW is the usual cause of a blank or half-broken dashboard after an update.
3. Do not cut power during the flash, and give it a couple of minutes to come back on its own before you touch anything.
4. Write down your pool settings first. A major version jump can clear them, and you will want to put the stratum URL, username and `x` password straight back.

After it is up, let it run a full hour, then compare the device's best-difficulty field against the pool again. If the number now behaves differently, that answers it. If it is still exactly 65.2k from boot, that is a very useful data point for JD and for the Discord thread.
